## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Textual reuse and alignment data from DharmaNexus demonstrate deep connections between the *Bāhirakathā* and the rest of the Pali Canon, identifying 3,645 matching passages shared across 189 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Substantial internal reuse occurs with Vinaya and Nikāya texts, most notably the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), *Citta Saṁyutta* (SN 41), *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), *Cammakkhandhaka* (Kd 5), and the subsequent *Paññattipañha* (Mil 3.1.1), as well as the commentary *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages of the text across languages with Sanskrit works including the *Mahāsannipātaratnaketudhāraṇīsūtra*, the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, and Asaṅga's *Yogācārabhūmi*, Chinese Āgama texts such as the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99), *Ekottarikāgama* (T 125), and *Madhyamāgama* (T 26), and Tibetan translations including the *Nandapravrajyāsūtra* and *Mahāsannipātaratnaketudhāraṇī* [DharmaNexus].
